title: Flutter trusted WebView activation, login and foreground TMS
prerequisites: Separately delivered compatible Flutter/native SDK artifacts and customer-configured AST/IDP connection.
Deployment-selected enrollment/login clients, signed assets and registration user.

Mandatory agent gate: before activation call sdk_deployment_preflight(mc_config_path, expected_mtls) using actual configuration and explicit customer deployment choice, never a sample default. Explicit-auth TMS always requires require_explicit_authentication=true and expected_token_client from observed token ownership. Set granted_scope_stage=current (default) for the existing token: missing tms warns/pends verification, NOT blocks, because SDK StartTransaction may acquire it through exchange/step-up. Set granted_scope_stage=explicit_auth for the actual resulting token: granted_scopes must contain tms, otherwise missing scope/evidence blocks. Requested/assigned scopes are not actual granted-token evidence. The tool verifies supplied metadata only (configuration_checked, runtime acceptance false), not issuer capability, live token validity or backend acceptance; no policy enforcement on independent raw service API calls.

Mandatory before a physical iOS install: sdk_ios_signing_preflight(app_path, expected_team_id, device_udid) must inspect the actual built .app signature, signer DER certificate membership in the profile, profile-authorized entitlements and target eligibility. Wildcard authorization is limited to verified Apple application/keychain identifier patterns; do not generalize wildcard matching to other entitlements. Keep customer signing-team preferences in local project configuration, never public defaults. No fallback team or install based only on project settings/build success; resolve mismatch/missing prerequisites first. Artifact-only checks without device_udid do not establish device eligibility. Do not uninstall an activated app to repair a cross-team update without the required data-preservation/removal authorization.
sequence:
## Mobile identity and AST registration

Android applicationId and iOS bundle identifier are mobile application identities.
AST app_name and its registered version identify backend registration records;
they are not automatically the same identifier. A new mobile bundle ID alone
neither proves an existing AST registration is incompatible nor proves it reusable.
Never recommend adopting the SuperApp mobile bundle ID just to reuse its assets.

For an authorized app integration, proceed with sdk_app_list, sdk_app_get and
sdk_app_versions without asking for another confirmation for these read-only
checks. Inspect the selected platform/version, registration user, lock state,
integrity policy, and any signing/package binding required by the supplied SDK
and deployment. If returned metadata cannot establish a required binding, identify
that exact gap; do not claim compatibility from the app name or integrity flag alone.
Reuse a suitable existing app/version and preserve its registration user and
security policy. Create new records only when none is suitable or the user requests
separate registration. Do not disable integrity to force reuse.

Do not assert that a delivered sdk_config.jwt is bound to a mobile package or AST
app/version without inspecting the documented configuration contract and applicable
claims privately. sdk_config_write in this MCP takes certificates and connection
service settings, not a mobile bundle ID or AST app_name. Obtain a fresh
backend-signed configuration when required; never edit signed JWT contents.

Preserve the user's previously selected test security policy and flow. Ask only
for an unresolved binding/policy choice or an actual blocker; do not request the
same decision repeatedly. A test selection is not a default for other customers.

## Signed configuration and retained choices
Within an authorized app build, request a fresh signed SDK configuration with
sdk_config_write using the selected environment service map and verified public
TLS certificates. Do not ask the user to supply a JWT or propose trying an
unverified sample JWT when the MCP can issue one. If certificates, permissions
or services are missing, report that concrete prerequisite; never disable TLS
verification or edit a signed configuration.
Read project instructions (including CLAUDE.md when present) for previously
selected test policy before asking again. Reuse an explicit current-project
ALLOW_VIRTUAL_SMART_CARD/device-PIN decision; do not extend that test choice to
other projects. This does not authorize changing shared backend security policy.

## Preferred integration path (user decision, 2026-09-29 validation round)

Trusted WebView enrollment and interactive login with SignedJWT token-based
returning login (useTokenBasedLogin=true, SE-signed JWT OfflineLogin) is the
primary documented path, protected by device biometrics/face recognition (iOS
biometric mode; Android BIOMETRIC_STRONG, no device-credential fallback).
PIN/password/no-authentication are alternatives, not defaults. On Android the
authentication policy is bound at Keystore key creation: decide the mode BEFORE
the key-creating activation step; changing it later requires discarding keys and
a fresh activation code.

mc_config compatibility on the qualified tuple (Android MCSDK 15.16.3088426 / iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231): the release rejects
SignedJWT combined with maverick.mKex=true or useSEKeyForSigningTransactions=true
with 800000279 ("Signed jwt together with mkex or SE for signing transactions is
not supported yet", Start NOT_SUPPORTED). The tested known-good SignedJWT
combination used mKex=false and useSEKeyForSigningTransactions=false
(runtime-verified on physical Android, 2026-09-29 validation round); a tested combination, not a
universal default.


Decision gate (Android PIN-prompt surprise, 2026-09-29 round): an explicit
authentication-mode decision is REQUIRED before activation. Activation guidance
or automation without a declared mode must produce a BLOCKING prompt/warning to
the user - never proceed on a silent default, because the first activation binds
the policy (on Android at Keystore key creation) and an unwanted mode costs an
uninstall plus a fresh activation code to undo. Authentication-mode enum values:
no=0, biometric=1, password=2, pin=3 (iOS 15.16 exposes no PIN mode). The
preferred method is biometric (user decision); record the chosen mode with the
run evidence.
# Flutter trusted WebView: activation, login and TMS

## Scope and evidence
Flutter wrapper 107.0.0 with hardening 21.0.0 was used for an Android mobile test app.
Android SDK startup, manual activation and foreground TMS approval were observed;
TMS acceptance was independently confirmed through AST status and result. The app
passed 26 unit/widget tests and Android builds. An unsigned iOS build passed before
the final environment/theme change; iOS device behavior is unverified. Returning
login can use cached or refreshed tokens: success alone does not prove a SignedJWT
grant. These observations qualify only this test tuple, not every delivery.

## Setup and activation
- Select a customer-configured connection explicitly. Keep server URLs, tenants,
  credentials and signed assets in project-local configuration, outside this recipe.
  Reuse an appropriate AST app/version and its existing registration user.
- Package the complete asset folder, referenced certificates and backend-signed
  SDK JWT. Isolate persistent SDK state per environment. Do not overwrite another
  environment's device binding when switching assets.
- This tested profile used useTokenBasedLogin=true, astServerBackend=maverick,
  AuthenticationMode.pin and maverick.jwtSignKeySecurityPolicy=
  ALLOW_VIRTUAL_SMART_CARD. This policy was explicitly selected for the test;
  it is not a universal default and must not silently replace a hardware policy.
- BDDKEnrollment/BDDKLogin can render HTML inside trusted WebView when the deployed
  clients support that contract. Inspect bindings and run sdk_native_preflight;
  passing preflight is not proof of fresh enrollment. Do not substitute SuperApp
  Login V2 or a generic browser flow that requires an already-registered device.
- Install warning/runtime/fatal listeners before Start. Gate all operations on
  successful Start/Restart and the returned state.
- GetAstClientDataEventT supplies clientData, astClientId and PKCE challenge/method.
  Preserve the wrapper's actual field spelling (107 uses codeChallange).
  Send X-KOBIL-ASTCLIENTDATA and forward X-KOBIL-ASTCLIENTID exactly as the SDK
  returns it, including the all-zero null ULID on fresh activation. Fresh
  enrollment may require X-KOBIL-ASTDEVICENAME. Returning WebView login requires
  X-KOBIL-ASTUSERID from the SDK user list, not the IDP UUID. Never fabricate IDs.
- Bind authorization requests to the selected client, redirect and PKCE values;
  validate redirect and state, and consume a code only once. Pass the returned
  code to SetAuthorisationCodeEventT with that same client/tenant and the selected
  authentication mode. A successful web page is not SDK activation success.
- Require SetAuthorisationCodeResult OK. Preserve data across restart and require
  the persisted user. OfflineLoginEventT handles token reuse/refresh and eligible
  SignedJWT login internally; use trusted WebView when interactive login is needed.
- Android device credential authentication needs FlutterFragmentActivity and the
  delivered biometric bridge initialized before its lifecycle callbacks. Flat AARs
  may require an explicit androidx.biometric dependency (tested 1.2.0-alpha03).
  Device PIN entry belongs to Android system UI, not chat or app text fields.

## Foreground TMS
1. Handle TriggerBanner, bind its payload/trace context, and show availability.
2. On Review send StartTransaction; display the exact DisplayConfirmationRequest
   transactionInformation and remaining time.
3. Handle a transaction PIN request separately from Android's device PIN. Return
   the actual user decision and exact information through DisplayConfirmation.
4. DisplayConfirmationResult is acknowledgement only. Wait for TransactionEnd,
   inspect status/error, and compare sdk_tms_status and sdk_tms_result.
5. Prevent duplicate decisions, late results reopening cancelled UI, and SDK
   restart while a transaction is active. Test deadlines with an injected clock.

Wrapper 107's inspected StartTransaction possibleResults list was empty, leaving
its Future unresolved. Verify the actual delivery; the app-local correction
includes DisplayConfirmationRequest, TransactionPinRequiredRequest,
TransactionTokenRequiredRequest and TransactionEnd. Keep the original delivery
unchanged and do not patch an unrelated wrapper version blindly.

freshness_seconds=0 requires fresh authentication; it does not disable freshness.
A synthetic test failed with status39/code516004035 and HTTP403 because its token
was older than the required time. An explicitly selected 300-second test window
then passed. Never relax a real transaction policy merely to make a test pass.

## Validation and diagnostics
Capture status, numeric error, description and report ID, without dumping event
objects or tokens. Never diagnose an enrollment HTTP406 from the status code alone: verified causes
include header-encoding defects (comma-joined ASTCLIENTDATA -> backend 513/4002
"Invalid AST Client ID") besides journey prerequisites. Inspect sanitized
POST/header propagation evidence (fragment counts, length ranges, character
classes - never values) before changing anything; never invent or drop AST headers.
An AST TMS HTTP202 is submission only; a pending result may return HTTP412.
Keep activation, returning login, observed SignedJWT grant, approve/reject/timeout,
push and iOS device results separate. Never automate approval of a real transaction.

## Exact trusted WebView authorization contract (unit-verified 2026-09-29, device retest pending)

Qualified tuple: Android MCSDK 15.16.3088426 / iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231,
Flutter delivery 549 (wrapper 106.0.0, kssidpdart 0.6.0), 2026-09-29 validation round.

- X-KOBIL-ASTCLIENTDATA encoding: the SDK returns clientData as a LIST of string
  fragments (1188 elements observed). The delivered kssidpdart 0.6.0 contract
  concatenates them with join() and NO separator. Comma-joining (join(',')) caused
  enrollment POST HTTP 406 with page error 513/4002 "Invalid AST Client ID".
  The no-separator encoding fix is unit-verified; the device retest is still
  pending, so do not claim runtime acceptance from the encoding fix alone.
- X-KOBIL-ASTCLIENTID: forward the SDK-provided value unchanged whenever it is a
  non-empty string, INCLUDING the all-zero null ULID on fresh activation. Historical
  branch evidence: omitting the header yields 513/4036; do not omit, rewrite or
  fabricate the ID to "fix" a 406.
- One PKCE pair per attempt: generate a single state/nonce/S256 code challenge per
  authorization attempt and keep it unchanged through the initial GET and the
  submit POST. Regenerate only for a genuinely new attempt.
- Redirect interception: validate the exact redirect scheme, host, effective port
  (explicit port or the scheme default), path AND the state parameter. Reject a
  redirect on a different port or foreign origin. Consume the authorization code
  exactly once, ignore duplicate callbacks after consumption, then hand the code to
  SetAuthorisationCode with the same client/tenant and selected authentication mode.
- Header propagation: headers passed to loadRequest apply to the initial GET; POST
  propagation is native WebView behavior. Verify with sanitized evidence, not
  assumptions.
- MANDATORY backend fixture readback before any retry: a failed enrollment can
  still consume the activation code and create a password credential or partial
  AST client. Read back your own fixture state (sdk_idp_user_credentials_list,
  sdk_ast_find_client, sdk_ast_device_list) before generating a new code or
  retrying a write.

Themes change presentation, not the SDK handshake. A copied client/flow may use
its own theme while the original BDDK definitions remain unchanged. Rendering a
new theme does not prove that its authentication submission succeeds.

## First-device test: trusted WebView and backend diagnostics

The delivered Flutter549 package contains wrapper106.0.0 and hardening20.1.0.
Source inspection confirms that its WebViewController.loadRequest defaults to
certPinningEnabled=false, pinnedCertificates="", and whiteList=[]. SDK Start
trust configuration is separate from this WebView proxy configuration. For the
selected trusted-WebView integration, explicitly pass the approved PEM trust
anchors, certPinningEnabled=true, and narrowly scoped full-URL allowlist patterns
derived from the deployment's approved HTTPS origins.
Verify the certificate chain and validity first; do not hardcode a public CA for
all customers, accept invalid certificates, or weaken pinning to make a page load.
Successful SDK Start/GetAstClientData does not prove WebView TLS is configured.

Install callbacks before loadRequest. Hardening20.1 RunTimeError exposes url,
errorCode and errorDescription. Retain numeric code, sanitized description,
origin (strip URL query/fragment/userinfo), phase and timestamp. Do not replace
these with only "WebView runtime error". Catch asset-read/loadRequest exceptions,
keep the outcome visible, and guard navigation completion against duplicate error,
redirect and cancellation callbacks. Never dump authorization URLs, headers or
entire error objects. SDK and WebView diagnostic channels are separate.

Use explicit checkpoints: SDK Start -> GetAstClientData -> WebView load -> IDP
redirect/state validation -> SetAuthorisationCode -> persisted-user restart/login.
If key exchange fails before navigation with an HTTP gateway/service error,
compare a bounded read-only sdk_backend_auth_test before changing WebView settings.
A failure in that phase cannot validate or invalidate a later WebView certificate
fix. Record actual status codes and server response; only diagnose a tunnel or
origin outage from supporting evidence. Do not repeatedly retry activation or
consume more codes during a backend outage. No successful page load or activation
is claimed until the corresponding phase has been observed after recovery.

Wrapper106 also maps StartTransaction to AsyncEventInfo([]), as does the inspected
107 delivery. Avoid awaiting a Future that has no terminal response mapping.
Use the documented event receiver with a bounded transaction state machine (and
handle dispatch failures), or a reviewed app-local mapping adapter. Global events
must still drive confirmation and TransactionEnd. An unawaited call alone is not
a complete fix. Do not modify the original supplied SDK delivery.

The mc_config maverick.jwtSignKeySecurityPolicy nesting has source evidence in
MCSDK configuration tests; binary string search alone does not establish nesting
or release compatibility. Preserve the selected policy and document the supplied
release's contract. When only newer source evidence exists, say so explicitly.

Log export acceptance requires reopening the ZIP, confirming nonempty expected
SDK log entries, and testing recipient access through the platform share flow.
Showing a share sheet alone does not establish successful delivery. iOS release
framework selection, hardening prerequisites and Android packaging warnings must
be checked against the actual delivery; a debug/unsigned build proves compilation
only, not production readiness or device feature acceptance.

### Trusted WebView allowlist matching

The Android trusted proxy matches each `whiteList` entry as a regular expression against the **complete URL** (`Pattern.matcher(url).matches()`), not just its origin. A bare `https://idp.example.com` therefore rejects `/auth/...`. Build a narrowly scoped pattern from the escaped configured origin, for example `'^${RegExp.escape(idpBaseUrl)}/.*\$'` in Dart. Never use an unrestricted wildcard or disable certificate verification to work around this.

`processReceivedSslError` checks both the proxy certificate and the URL allowlist. If logs say `Proxy set up is correct` followed by `certificate verification failed`, inspect the allowlist before replacing certificates. The latter message alone does not prove a certificate-chain failure.

## Mobile certificate-chain coverage and pinning diagnostics (verified 2026-09-29, Android MCSDK 15.16.3088426 / iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231)

SDK Start trust (mc_config iam.trustedSslServerCerts, passed to the version-specific
Start API) is SEPARATE from WebView proxy trust (Flutter pinnedCertificates/
certPinningEnabled; iOS KsTrustedWebViewConfiguration.certsDataForValidation).
Configure and verify both independently, matching each API's expected DER/PEM
contract. NEVER disable certificate or hostname verification.

The mobile TLS client may negotiate or build a DIFFERENT chain than desktop
verification. Verified on iOS (simulator and physical device, 2026-09-29): for a
Let's Encrypt chain, iOS builds the chain to the self-signed system root
ISRG Root X2, while desktop verification sees ISRG Root X1 via the cross-sign.
Pinning X1 alone produces KS_CERTIFICATE_ERROR (onURLBlocked reason 1, subsystem
1500000, log line "servercert validation endresult failed") even though SecTrust
itself succeeds. Fix: pin the authentic X2 (taken from the system root store and
fingerprint-checked) ALONGSIDE X1 - do not weaken pinning.

Derive approved trust anchors from the chains actually negotiated by the mobile
TLS clients on each target platform; never hard-code one CA for all environments,
and never assume one observed chain applies everywhere.

Pinning diagnostics on iOS: KsTrustedWebView.setLogListener plus
KsTwvLog.setLogLevel(debug) - temporarily, remove after diagnosis - shows the
per-certificate validation steps.

The Android trusted-proxy full-URL allowlist matching fix (anchored escaped-origin
regex, see the allowlist section) is already part of this knowledge pack; a
KS_CERTIFICATE_ERROR is not automatically that allowlist issue nor automatically a
chain issue - check both with the actual logs.

Preflight before every device round: run sdk_tls_chain_check with the
environment hosts and the exact certsDataForValidation / trustedSslServerCerts
asset the app will ship. An X1-only asset against the akinci-style
leaf<-YE2<-Root YE<-ISRG Root X2 serving is reported as missing X2 BEFORE a
phone is touched (VAL-16/VAL-36). The tool only reads served chains; it never
disables pinning or verification.

### Preserve the selected themed clients

Before choosing enrollment/login client IDs, read the current project choices and
inspect the deployed clients' login_theme, browser-flow bindings and redirect URIs.
When the user selected a styled copy of a working flow, retain those client IDs in
both the WebView request and SDK IAM configuration. Do not revert to BDDK-named
example clients merely because this recipe uses them as a reference: those may
select a different theme. Keep the original flow unchanged. Rendering the selected
theme verifies presentation only; test authentication and SDK completion separately.
expected_result: SDK activation and returning login verified separately; terminal TMS result matches backend outcome.
failure_handling: Read warning/runtime/fatal explanations before retrying. Do not infer activation from web success or approval from HTTP202.
Keep current deployment policy; never invent AST IDs, substitute SuperApp V2 or export IAM tokens into Dart.

Android trusted WebView whiteList entries are full-URL regular expressions. Escape the configured HTTPS origin and permit its path; a bare origin rejects /auth/... . Keep certificate pinning enabled. If Proxy set up is correct precedes certificate verification failed, inspect the URL allowlist: processReceivedSslError combines both checks, so that message alone does not establish a certificate-chain failure.

800000279 at Start: unsupported SignedJWT + mKex/SE-signing combination in mc_config. Set maverick.mKex=false and useSEKeyForSigningTransactions=false for the SignedJWT path on the qualified 15.16 tuple (runtime-verified, 2026-09-29 validation round); preserve the numeric error fields and check the device log — the explanation may appear only in native logs.

Enrollment HTTP 406 with 513/4002: check ASTCLIENTDATA fragment concatenation (no separator per kssidpdart 0.6.0) and that the SDK ASTCLIENTID (null ULID included) was forwarded unchanged, before touching clients or flows. Encoding fix unit-verified 2026-09-29; device retest pending.
Before retrying a failed enrollment, read back the fixture: the activation code may be consumed and a password credential or partial AST client created even though the SDK reported failure.

KS_CERTIFICATE_ERROR / onURLBlocked reason 1 / subsystem 1500000 "servercert validation endresult failed": the pinned set did not cover the mobile-negotiated chain (verified iOS: ISRG Root X2 system root vs desktop X1 cross-sign, 2026-09-29). Pin the fingerprint-checked authentic X2 alongside X1; never disable validation or hostname checks. Never blank-fail the WebView (VAL-36, 2026-09-29): the X1-only pinning failure on Flutter iOS rendered a SILENT white/blank page with no user-visible error, and the gap was only found by chain inspection. In the reference integration a blank page must be IMPOSSIBLE: wire onWebResourceError/onWebResourceHttpError (Flutter NavigationDelegate), the trusted-WebView failure callbacks (onURLBlocked/KS_CERTIFICATE_ERROR, load-failure delegate methods) and every TLS-failure path to a visible in-app diagnostic view that replaces the WebView content and shows the numeric error code, the phase and a sanitized hint (for example 'certificate validation failed - check the pinned trust anchors'), never URLs, hostnames, tokens or other secrets. Surfacing the error never means weakening or disabling validation. Tests must force a trust failure and assert the diagnostic view appears instead of a blank page.

Dart sanitizer/redaction defects can swallow SDK errors (2026-09-29 validation round, kssidpdart 0.6.0): the inline (?i) flag is INVALID in Dart RegExp and throws FormatException at construction, so the diagnostic path itself fails and hides the SDK error. Use RegExp(pattern, caseSensitive: false) and EXECUTE sanitizers in tests against representative errors and secret-bearing inputs. Redaction invariant: the numeric SDK status/errorCode/type and the sanitized description must survive secret redaction - keep the numeric code under a distinct key such as errorCode outside the redaction boundary; a redactor matching generic 'code=' fields erased error evidence. UI/test automation must filter credential-bearing fields before emitting output; never log plaintext credentials or authorization URLs.

Toolchain surprises during long Flutter builds (2026-09-29 round): a half-installed Android NDK failed mid-build (VAL-06; local NDK 27.2.12479018 compiled - a local workaround, not vendor qualification) and the iOS Runner/Pods deployment target had to be raised to iOS 15 for Xcode 27 during compilation (VAL-07). Run a local toolchain preflight first (complete NDK, supported compilers, deployment target vs installed Xcode, signing/device readiness incl. ON-DEVICE trust of the signing team - a Developer App Certificate trust failure appears only at LAUNCH while install and codesign verify pass silently (VAL-35), disk space) and never mutate shared toolchains automatically.

Encrypted-file-logging capability matrix per SDK family x platform (2026-09-29 validation round): classic MCSDK 15.16 Android = SUPPORTED (logs_mPower written, runtime-observed); classic MCSDK 15.16 Swift iOS = SUPPORTED (validated); shift delivery 549 Flutter/Android (ksmastercontrollerwrapperdart 106.0.0, libnb.so core) = NOT WRITING - it accepts logsStorageDirectory at init but writes ZERO encrypted log files even at LogDebug (VAL-34, open vendor question; H-LOG-1 stands after the H-LOG-2 probe refuted the last public knob); shift 549 Flutter/iOS = SUPPORTED (validated 2026-09-29 on device: 3 encrypted log files, ~696 KB, CRC-clean ZIP with manifest, zero plaintext hits; VAL-38 - same delivery writes logs on iOS but not Android, so the VAL-34 defect is Android-platform-specific in the shift core). Acceptance runners must mark a known NOT-WRITING gap as EXPECTED-FAIL instead of probing the device again; an EXPECTED-FAIL is not a pass and does not close the vendor question. Update this matrix only from runtime evidence on the exact delivery, never by assuming family parity.

When SDK reports FAILED/errorCode=0 and no Warning/RuntimeError/FatalError, inspect sanitized native SDK and HTTP diagnostics; listener silence is not absence of an error. Distinguish issuer TLS_CLIENT_WITH_KEY rejection 510000015 (mTLS deployment mismatch), HTTP403 Client is not the holder of the token wrapped as 700000022 (token holder versus IAM exchange client), missing explicit tms scope 516004034, and freshness failure 516004035. Numeric wrappers alone do not establish the cause; retain operation/status/explanation without tokens.

Swift trusted-WebView callbacks: inspect the delivered return/decision semantics and cancel only the verified authorization redirect. Do not cancel all nonredirect/external navigation; preserve the existing allowlist and certificate checks. Query versus fragment response parsing is scoped to the selected verified journey, never a reason to broaden endpoint/state validation or substitute another themed client/flow.
checklist: SDK startup and complete packaged assets verified.
SetAuthorisationCode succeeds after enrollment.
Persisted user and returning login succeed after restart.
SignedJWT grant independently observed if claimed.
TMS approve, reject and timeout tested independently against backend results.
iOS device and push delivery tested separately.
Mobile bundle/package identity and AST app/version are distinguished; reuse decision is supported by registration, integrity and applicable binding evidence.
WebView proxy trust anchors, pinning and allowed origins configured independently from SDK Start.
WebView failures preserve numeric error, sanitized explanation and phase; duplicate callbacks and load failures handled.
Forced trust/load failure shows the sanitized in-app diagnostic view (numeric code + hint, no URLs or secrets) instead of a blank page; a blank page is impossible in the reference integration.
Backend failure before navigation is distinguished from WebView TLS failure; recovery retested.
Exported ZIP reopened and receiving-app access verified.
Trusted WebView full-URL allowlist permits the intended authentication path and rejects other origins; certificate pinning remains enabled.
Failed result events and ConnectionManagerError inspected alongside Warning/RuntimeError/FatalError; actual log destination checked before export.

AST header construction matches the delivered wrapper contract: clientData fragments concatenated without separator; SDK ASTCLIENTID (including the null ULID) forwarded unchanged; one PKCE state/nonce/S256 pair kept through GET and POST.
Redirect interception validates exact scheme/host/effective port/path plus state, rejects different-port redirects, consumes the code once and ignores duplicate callbacks.
Backend fixture state (credentials, AST client) read back before any enrollment retry or new activation code.
Pinned trust anchors cover the chains actually negotiated by the mobile TLS clients (SDK Start trust and WebView trust verified separately); no verification disabled.

Sanitizers executed in tests: valid Dart RegExp flags (no inline (?i)), no throw on representative errors, numeric errorCode/type and sanitized description survive secret redaction, credential-bearing UI fields filtered before any emitted output.

Authentication mode explicitly decided and recorded before activation (enum no=0, biometric=1, password=2, pin=3; preferred biometric); a missing decision produced a blocking prompt, not a silent default.
